steps.body: Each year the county publishes one total rate for this school district. That published total is what this app charts for this row.

sources.text: County mill levy hub (all year PDFs)

steps.title: Ballot Issue 4A: More operating money
steps.body: Issue 4A asked for a tax increase of $9 million for 2025 (and more in later years, within state limits). The ballot said the rate could not jump by more than one mill in any one year. The money was for school needs listed on the ballot, such as safety staff, teachers, mental health support, and classroom technology.

steps.title: Ballot Issue 4B: Borrowing for buildings
steps.body: The same ballot asked voters to let the district borrow up to $950 million for school buildings and related work (with a repayment cost capped at $1.85 billion, and annual taxes to repay the debt capped at $99.9 million). Approving the loan is not the same as saying those building costs already make up today's published total rate. Bonds may be sold over time.

steps.title: What Arapahoe County reports for 4A and 4B
steps.body: These are the county's published vote counts for both issues. This app reports what that record says; it does not independently verify election administration.

steps.title: What the school district's own budget says
steps.body: The district's adopted budget for 2025-26 says local property tax includes $9 million of new money (described there as 1 mill) from an increase the budget calls voter-approved. That is the district explaining its own budget. It is not the same document as the county's one-number total rate for this row.
